The two sleds are field-replaceable modules - the guide has a Sled Removal and Installation procedure and ships a blank cover for an unused slot - so each front slot is a bay that accepts edgecore/amx-3200-sled400@1 or edgecore/amx-3200-sled-blank@1, and the ports live on the sled, addressed sled-1/module/port-3 and so on. The slots read x 59.03-242.81 and 247.53-431.7 on the guide's front, 183.8 wide on a 188.5 pitch; the chassis prints SLED1 and SLED2 on the narrow strips to the right of each. THE PORTS' OPTICS AND MODES ARE ON THE SLED'S CONTRACT, not in this device's attrs: every traffic port lives on an AMX-3200-SLED400, and a device-level optics key names no port group of the device's own."},"chassis":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"DATASHEET 'Dimensions (WxDxH): 438.4 mm x 430 mm x 43.5 mm' and the guide's '438.4 x 430 x 43.5 mm (17.26 x 16.93 x 1.71 in.)'. Two documents, one triple; 438.4 is the body."},"figure-choice":{"confidence":"measured","note":"Gate 1. THE GUIDE'S FRONT SETS THE FRONT: panel 1114 x 111 px, aspect -0.42% against 438.4/43.5, 2.541 px/mm on x and 2.552 on y. Two standard apertures confirm the scale independently - the QSFP28 openings measure 18.50 against the registry's 18.50 and the CFP2 openings 41.7-42.1 x 12.54 against the MSA's 41.5 x 12.4. The guide's REAR is -1.48% on aspect, so every rear number is checked against the two straight-on rear photographs, and they agree on the fan pitch to 0.05 mm. The datasheet's front photograph is taken from above and is used for what it alone shows - the printed port numbering and the lamp windows - not for geometry."},"management-panel":{"confidence":"measured","note":"MEASURED on the guide's front at 5x and matched to the straight-on photograph: the RS-232 console RJ-45 at the top left over the 1G SFP out-of-band port ('CONSOLE up down SFP'); the 1000BASE-T MGMT RJ-45 over a USB-A ('MGMT up down USB'); the Edge-core wordmark above them; the 4 mm banana receptacle, the guide's callout 2, at the top right - which is the ESD wrist-strap jack, common/esd-jack@1, whose own provenance identifies the equipment-side ESD point as exactly a 4 mm banana; two gold coaxial 1PPS jacks labelled SLED1-1PPS and SLED2-1PPS, one per sled; and four rectangular system lamps across the foot - PSU, DIAG, FAN, LOC - over the model name. Honeycomb vents run down the left edge and along the bottom. THE MGMT JACK IS LAMPED AND THE CONSOLE IS NOT: 'MGMT LEDs: Left: Green (link/act), Right: Green (1G speed)', and nothing for the console - L76's convention too."},"numbering":{"confidence":"photo-measured","note":"THE PHOTOGRAPH AND THE GUIDE NUMBER THE SLED DIFFERENTLY. The datasheet's photograph prints CFP2-1, CFP2-2 and then 3 up 4 down ... 9 up 10 down: each sled numbered 1-10 with its line ports first. The guide's line art prints the client ports 1-8. This device follows the photograph, which is of the hardware; see the gap. Supplies (PSU2 left, PSU1 right) and fans (5 to 1 from the left) are numbered from one, as the rear prints them."},"rear":{"confidence":"photo-measured","note":"Measured on the guide's rear and on both rear photographs. PSU2 at x 14.3 and PSU1 at 350.6, each 73.5 x 40.0; five fan trays from x 97.0 on a 50.45 pitch; each module's label printed vertically in the web to its RIGHT with an arrow pointing back at it - 'PSU2', '5' ... '1', 'PSU1'. The protective earth is a single stud under an earth symbol on the strip at the far left; the guide asks for a #8 AWG wire to it."},"sources":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"Two documents and six product photographs. amx3200-datasheet (the AMX3200 coherent transponder and muxponder data sheet) carries the spec list, a 2000 px product photograph of the front taken from slightly above, and an ordering table that - unusually for this vendor - names the FRUs: AMX-3200-SLED400, AMX-3200-FAN, AMX-3200-AC-PSU and AMX-3200-48V-PSU, with the supply's 73.5 mm width and the fans' 40.5 mm size. amx3200-qsg (the 400G Transponder and Muxponder AMX3200 quick start guide, four pages) carries line-art front and rear elevations, the Overview callouts and the FRU procedures.
